summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, severe asthma, and chronic abdominal pain was admitted for an asthma exacerbation and worsening epigastric pain. He had not followed up with specialists after a recent intubation for asthma. Initial management included bronchodilators and steroids for asthma. Abdominal pain persisted despite normal CT and ultrasound; an EGD revealed candidal esophagitis and CMV-positive gastric ulcers, leading to treatment with fluconazole and valganciclovir. An MRCP showed cirrhosis and a 6.2 cm liver nodule concerning for dysplastic changes or early malignancy, necessitating outpatient hepatology follow-up for biopsy. Asthma improved with therapy, and he was discharged home on multiple new medications with plans for pulmonology, ID, and GI follow-up. He committed to sobriety and adherence to care.
